sections.html: An estimated 239,593 people lived in Clay County in mid-2025, 9.8% above the 218,249 counted at the start of 2020. The typical owned home is worth $312,500, and owners occupy 75.9% of the 94,791 housing units. Rent runs about $1,551. Steady growth and a high owner share mean a lot of sellers hold capped assessments, and their buyers start from a fresh value.

Two offices split the work. One office mails the bills and collects payment. The other sets each parcel's value and decides who qualifies for an exemption.

Mailing is done by November 1. If a lender pays your tax, you receive an information-only copy. Value is set as of January 1, though payment is normally due starting November 1. Florida Statute 197.122 puts the burden on owners to find out what they owe and pay before delinquency, even when no bill arrives in the mail.

  • Property appraiser: value, homestead, portability and other exemptions, filed by March 1.
  • Tax collector: payment, installment and partial payment plans, certificate sales.
  • Clerk: records the deed and collects stamp tax.

The discount begins at 4% in November and drops a point a month to 1% in February. March carries none, and April 1 brings delinquency.

Clay County billing calendar
Pay inResult
NovemberLargest discount, 4%
DecemberOne point less, 3%
January2%
FebruarySmallest discount, 1%
MarchGross amount
April 1Delinquent, with a 3% penalty
May 1Further fees apply
By June 1Certificate sale

Every payment method is accepted. A card payment adds a 2.50% fee, and an online e-check adds none.

To use installments, apply by April 30 with estimated taxes above $100, then pay the first quarter by June 30.

The first installment carries a 6% discount. A July payment earns no discount, and missing July 31 cancels the plan. The second, due September 30, carries 4.5%. The third, due December 31, carries 3%, and the fourth, due March 31, carries none. Last year's notice drives the first two payments, and the final two absorb any change in ownership, value or exemptions.

Partial payments are a separate option under Florida Statute 197.374. The owner submits a Partial Payment Plan application with the first payment or in person, and payments can begin November 1. Online payment isn't accepted for this plan. Early payment discounts are forfeited, so the full March amount is due, and any balance left on April 1 is delinquent and goes into the June certificate sale.

Expect a 3% penalty on April 1, more fees from May 1, and a certificate sale by June 1.

If a certificate sits unredeemed, a tax deed application can follow two years on, with a $75 application fee. The clerk conducts the auction. The owner can pay the taxes before the deed issues and stop the sale.

Costs climb at each stage, so request a payoff before you put a house with unpaid tax on the market.

Three dates deserve attention during a listing, in winter or summer. March 1 is the exemption filing deadline for any buyer who wants homestead in the first year. March 31 is the final due date for a full bill or the fourth installment, and April 1 starts the penalty clock.

The installment plan also has a July trap. A first payment that misses June 30 but lands before July 31 earns no discount, and missing July 31 cancels the plan and returns the owner to the regular due dates and discounts. If you close in summer, find out which installments are paid so the contract divides the rest fairly.

A value petition filed with the clerk is due 25 days after the TRIM notice, and an exemption denial carries a 30 day window. Read the TRIM notice each August.

  • Application for installments: April 30.
  • Credit card fee: 2.50%, none for online e-check.
  • Partial payment: current year only, November 1 through March 31.

sections.h2: Homestead and the Save Our Homes cap
sections.html:
Send Form DR-501 to the appraiser by March 1. The home has to be your permanent residence on January 1.

The exemption can be worth as much as $50,000. The first $25,000 reduces all taxes, and the added $25,000 reduces only non-school taxes on value over $50,000. After the first year, assessed value rises by no more than 3 percent or inflation, whichever is lower. The published chart lists caps of 2.9 percent for 2025 and 2.7 percent for 2026. Portability allows a move to a new Florida homestead within three years, with Form DR-501T filed alongside.

Non-homestead property has a separate 10 percent annual limit on assessed value growth. A rental or second home can still see its taxable value climb every year.

sections.h2: Settling the tax when you sell
sections.html:
At closing the agent apportions the year's tax, subtracts any balance from your proceeds and sends the deed to the clerk for recording, which is when stamp tax is collected.

A deed carries a stamp tax of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration everywhere except Miami-Dade, and the state revenue agency holds all parties to the document liable no matter who agrees to pay. Confirm which tax year your payoff covers, because partial payment rules apply to the current year only.

With a lender-held escrow, find out when any refund would arrive, and check with the collector that this year's bill is settled.

Start with a written payoff from the collector, and ask whether any plan is open on the parcel. Next, tell the title agent which installments are paid so the contract can split the rest. Then check that your exemption paperwork is in order so you can explain it to the buyer. On closing day, read the settlement statement's tax lines against the collector's figure, and afterward file the paid receipt with your closing documents.

A cash buyer doesn't need a lender's approval, so closings can move fast. That makes it more useful to settle the payoff early, since there is less time to fix a surprise.

If you inherited the house, bring the paperwork that shows you may sell it, and tell the collector where to send future notices. If the property is a rental, collect your tenant's contact details so the buyer can reach them. Ask your title agent for a list of documents it needs from you well before the closing date, and gather them in one folder. Having each item in hand keeps a sale on schedule even if a tax question comes up late. Finally, save an email or letter from the collector confirming your balance, so any later question about the same year can be answered with a document and not a memory. Store it with your deed copy and closing statement.

faqs.q: What are the Clay County property tax discounts?
faqs.a: Four points off in November, shrinking monthly through February. March pays the full amount, and April 1 starts delinquency with a 3% penalty.

faqs.q: When is the Clay County installment application due?
faqs.a: Apply by the end of April, with an estimate above $100. The June 30 first payment gets the biggest discount.

faqs.q: Is there a card fee on Clay County tax payments?
faqs.a: A card adds 2.50%. Online e-check payments carry none.

faqs.q: When is the Clay County tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: By June 1, covering the prior year's delinquent real estate taxes, with extra fees from May 1.

faqs.q: Who takes the Clay County homestead application?
faqs.a: Use Form DR-501 and send it to the appraiser by the first of March. The collector only bills.
